Singapore AI Safety Hub is hiring for their AI verification team. SASH is a Singapore-based research institute and fieldbuilder aiming to facilitate collaboration between Eastern and Western AI governance communities.  Our verification team focuses on prototyping tools which could be used to verify agreements about AI deployment or training, and demonstrates them to policymakers, AI company employees, and researchers. Thus far, we've briefed government officials and defence personnel on AI verification -- including from the US, China, Singapore, and Australia. Read more about our work <https://www.aisafety.sg/blog/making-ai-verification-international|here>.
We're hiring for a <https://www.aisafety.sg/careers/research-engineer-ai-verification|Research Engineer> and <https://www.aisafety.sg/careers/technical-lead-ai-verification|Technical Lead> to expand our prototyping efforts.
• *Technical Lead — USD 120,000–180,000:* Set technical direction, manage engineers, and lead development of verification prototypes.
• *Research Engineer -- USD 90,000 --150,000:* Build prototypes spanning ML engineering, cybersecurity, confidential computing, hardware, and demos.
• *Location:* Remote, Singapore, or London.

If you missed out on the MATS DC field trip, there is now another opportunity for funded travel to DC, courtesy of Constellation's Generator program. They're actively looking for past and current MATS fellows to apply!

*****

*Apply by August 16: <http://www.longitudepolicy.org/|Longitude DC Intensive>, Oct 5 – 14*
The Longitude DC Intensive is a fully funded, eight-day AI policy program in Washington, DC. It's designed for people with a technical AI safety background to explore how they could contribute to the AI policy ecosystem.
*What?*
• Eight days of talks, workshops and networking with DC AI policy organizations and professionals to learn and explore where and how your technical expertise is needed in the policy ecosystem
• Travel, housing and meals are covered
• More info: <http://longitudepolicy.org|longitudepolicy.org>
*When?*
October 5 to 14, 2026, Washington, DC
*Why?*
We want to make it as easy as possible for technical AI safety researchers to explore whether they should work in policy roles.
The AI policy ecosystem has difficulty sourcing people who deeply understand AI and can do technical work to inform policymakers. At Longitude, we think it's very important that these high-leverage roles get filled - they range from developing and running evaluations to advising policy professionals on how to handle warning shots like the Hugging Face incident.
*<http://longitude.fillout.com/apply?ref=mats|Apply here by August 16> or <http://longitude.fillout.com/refer|refer someone who should apply>!*

BlueDot:
> Announcing Incubator Week v5 — now in San Francisco :bridge_at_night:
> 
> Most accelerators take 12 weeks to validate a business. We take five days to break what's standing between you and launching an impactful AI safety org - a co-founder, a threat model, a first customer, a funder commit. You name it on Monday in falsifiable terms, and then go on to pressure-test it all week - with us, with the cohort, with experts.
> 
> On Friday you pitch to us and funders we bring into the room. If we back your idea, we'll fund immediate needs on the spot - and give you up to $100k within two weeks if you make good progress.
> 
> Last cohort, people found co-founder leads through cold outreach mid-week, others killed their ideas by Wednesday and left with something better. They walked out with live funding conversations and have raised more than $500k from Coefficient Giving and Longview since June.
> 
> We are looking for people in or adjacent to AI safety, biosecurity, cyber, or other catastrophic-risk fields, ready to drop what they're doing to build a high-impact org. You don't (yet) need a polished idea - you need a problem you can't put down, and a good enough model of the space to get started in it. We'll help with the rest.
> 
> If that's you, apply <https://airtable.com/appnJbsG1eWbAdEvf/pagA7JU8pPkkbDCOJ/form|here> by August 7th - all expenses (flights, hotel, meals) covered.
> 
> Know someone who should be there? Refer them <https://airtable.com/appnJbsG1eWbAdEvf/pagzDBxQxLCuU2A1i/form|here> - we will send you $2,000 for each accepted referral.

Take a close look at this!  AE Studio (another one of our career fair attendees) has two alignment roles and a fellowship (note: applications close Aug 17)

1. FT roles:

*AE Studio is currently hiring for two alignment roles.*

AE does frontier alignment research on neglected approaches, paired with production-grade research engineering, alongside collaborators from Anthropic, Redwood Research, Princeton, Los Alamos National Laboratory, and other orgs.

Recent work includes 3 papers at ICML this year, including a spotlight on GRAM, a pretraining method developed with Anthropic that isolates dangerous knowledge into modules that can be switched on or off at deployment.

*Alignment Scientist / Engineer.* For high-agency technical generalists who want real ownership of ambitious research directions that others neglect, like pre-training interventions, novel interpretability, and neuroscience-inspired alignment.
Role and application: <https://grnh.se/lpr5zjy34us|grnh.se/…>

*Alignment Research Manager.* For people who would rather run the research process than do hands-on research, handling prioritization, experiment tracking, and keeping teams moving alongside the researchers setting direction.
Role and application: <https://grnh.se/kvw542794us|grnh.se/kvw542794us>

Both are remote-first, with team members working either out of the LA office or fully remote, focusing on promising but neglected problems with funding behind them and none of the incentives of an AGI race.

2. Fellowship:

Another opportunity that might fit this group well. The *AIAF Fellowship* is an 8-week paid alignment research program run by the AI Alignment Foundation in partnership with AE Studio, and applications recently opened.

Fellows work full-time on neglected approaches to alignment with AE Studio's research team. A dedicated research manager works with the team daily, AE researchers set the research direction, and there's a midpoint 1:1 with AIAF or AE alignment leadership. Every team works toward a LessWrong post, and a paper when the research supports it, ending with a hybrid Demo Day in LA (with travel covered for those who can make the trip).

- *$12,000 stipend* for the 8 weeks, fully remote
- *Compute and API credits covered* per team
- *6 spots*, reviewed individually

Worth a look if you're between programs and want another block of funded research time with people who will push your direction. Any career stage, and people moving into alignment from other technical fields are explicitly in scope.

Applications close *August 17 (AoE)* and the program starts September 8: <https://bit.ly/4wAXuU7|bit.ly/4wAXuU7>

We are looking for *2 collaborators* for the project, <https://verifiedmechanisms.ai/|Formally verified autoresearch for theoretical mechanistic interpretability>.

The goal is to build theoretical foundations for mechanistic interpretability by asking how far frontier models can go in discovering and proving theorems about the internal computations of transformers. We are looking for a <https://verifiedmechanisms.ai/careers/research-scientist/|research scientist> to work on the mechanistic interpretability side, and a <https://verifiedmechanisms.ai/careers/research-engineer/|research engineer> to design the multi-agent harness for autoresearch. Both roles are part-time (10-15 hours/week) from September to November 2026, with a stipend of at least $1,000/month plus Claude Max and ChatGPT Pro subscriptions. You can find the details for the <https://verifiedmechanisms.ai/careers/research-scientist/|research scientist> and <https://verifiedmechanisms.ai/careers/research-engineer/|research engineer> roles here.

If you're interested in the mathematics of transformers, multi-agent orchestration, or autoresearch, you are strongly encouraged to apply. Applications are open until *August 15.* 

Excited about this research direction? We would be happy to hear from you. Apply <https://forms.gle/91UeZhJex4sf841R6|here> to join the project!

Next iteration of AI Security Bootcamp is now open! Week-long SF educational intensive, meals and accommodation provided

AI Security Bootcamp explores the rapidly evolving threat landscape of frontier AI systems, equipping security professionals with the knowledge and hands-on skills to secure against current and emerging risks.

As AI systems become more capable and integrated into critical infrastructure, new attack surfaces and failure modes are emerging that traditional security training doesn't cover. This program is designed to fill that gap with an intensive, practitioner-focused curriculum that prepares participants to engage with the most pressing AI security challenges we see today, and to grapple with how the risks will evolve in the future.

Participants complete pre-work before the program to establish baseline ML fundamentals, followed by an immersive week delivered through demos, lectures, guest speakers, and hands-on red/blue team exercises that build skills across the modern AI system stack.
